record.title: Skew blow-up conjecture for triangle densities
record.statement:
Let $B=K_{a,b,c}$ be a blowup of the triangle, where $a,b,c$ are positive integers not all equal. Let $f_B(\gamma)$ denote the minimum possible $B$-density in a graph of triangle density $\gamma$.

**Skew blow-up conjecture.** There is a constant $c>0$ such that

$$
f_B(\gamma)\leq \gamma^{\frac13(ab+bc+ac)+c}.
$$

This predicts that the random graph does not minimize the density of a skewed blowup. The construction in the paper verifies related cases, including bounds for $K_{1,1,t}$ up to an $o(1)$ term, but the general assertion remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Asaf Shapira and Raphael Yuster, “On the Density of a Graph and its Blowup”, arXiv:0903.0198 (2009).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.0198

record.title: Conjecture on bounded-length zero-sum subsequences
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite Abelian group of exponent $m$, and let $\eta_{\ell m}(G)$ be the smallest positive integer $t$ such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least $t$ contains a non-empty zero-sum subsequence of length at most $\ell m$. **Bounded-length zero-sum conjecture.** If $S$ is a sequence over $G$ with $|S|=\eta_{\ell m}(G)+i-1$, where $i\in\llbracket 1,\ell m\rrbracket$, then $S$ contains a zero-sum subsequence $S'$ satisfying 
$$
i\leq |S'|\leq \ell m.
$$
 This is the paper's second concluding conjecture and is intended to refine the extremal information encoded by $\eta_{\ell m}(G)$; the source presents it as open.
record.source_name: Benjamin Girard, “On the existence of zero-sum subsequences of distinct lengths”, arXiv:0903.3458 (2012).

**Sufficiency conjecture.** The linear equations, near-symmetry equations and special values determine the numbers $\hat{A}_{n,i,j}$ uniquely.

record.title: Hamiltonicity conjecture for minimum-degree-three random graphs
record.statement: Let $G_{n,cn}$ be the random graph on $n$ vertices with $cn$ edges, conditioned on having minimum degree at least $3$. **Hamiltonicity conjecture.** For any $c\geq 3/2$, $G_{n,cn}$ has a Hamilton cycle with high probability as $n$ tends to infinity. This conjecture proposes that average degree at least $3$ suffices for Hamiltonicity in the random graph conditioned on minimum degree $3$; the supplied text gives no resolution beyond the preceding result that $128n$ edges suffice.

record.title: The convergence conjecture for the branching-random-walk maximum
record.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the maximum at generation $n$ in the branching random walk considered in the paper, and let $b_n$ be its deterministic centering term. **Branching-random-walk convergence conjecture.** There is a random variable $X$ with continuous distribution such that

$$
B_n-b_n\to X\qquad\text{as }n\to\infty.
$$

The paper notes that convergence in probability of this centered maximum is known under certain displacement-law conditions, but is not known for the model arising from Pratt trees.

record.title: The minimum-light-number gap conjecture for trees with loops
record.statement:
Let $G$ be obtained from a tree by adding some loops. The quantities $ML(G)$ and $ML^*(G)$ denote the minimum light numbers of the sigma-game and lit-only sigma-game on $G$, respectively.

**Tree gap conjecture.**

$$
ML^*(G)-ML(G)\in \{0,1\}.
$$

This conjecture concerns how much the lit-only restriction can increase the minimum light number. The paper gives a general upper bound of $2$ for the corresponding configuration-wise difference on these graphs, with sharpness, but the stated conjecture remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Categoricity conjecture for the analytic Zariski structure of generic complex Abelian varieties
record.statement: Let $\A$ be a generic complex Abelian variety defined over a number field, and let $\Ax(\A(\C) \times \Cm)$ be the analogously defined $\lww$-class. A **generic Abelian-variety categoricity conjecture.** The class $\Ax(\A(\C) \times \Cm)$ is analytic Zariski, excellent, and categorical in uncountable cardinalities. A sufficient condition is that the Mumford–Tate group of $\A$ is the symplectic group, namely the largest possible Mumford–Tate group. This conjecture concerns the model-theoretic structure associated with covers of Abelian varieties and proposes strong categoricity properties for generic varieties; the supplied text does not provide evidence resolving it.

record.title: Almost Reducibility Conjecture for analytic cocycles
record.statement:
Let $(\alpha,A)$ be an analytic cocycle, and let $A_\epsilon$ denote its complexified cocycle at imaginary shift $\epsilon$. Assume that $L(\alpha,A_\epsilon)=0$ for $a<\epsilon<b$. A holomorphic cocycle is **almost reducible** if it can be conjugated arbitrarily close to the identity on every strictly smaller complex strip. **Almost Reducibility Conjecture.** Regularity with zero Lyapunov exponents implies almost reducibility. More precisely, for every $n$ there exists a holomorphic map

$$
B_n:\{a+1/n<|\operatorname{Im} z|<b-1/n\}\to\operatorname{SL}(2,\mathbb{C})
$$

such that

$$
\|B_n(z+\alpha)A(z)B(z)^{-1}-\operatorname{id}\|<1/n
$$

for $a+1/n<\operatorname{Im} z<b-1/n$. Moreover, if $a=-b$ and $A$ is real-symmetric, then each $B_n$ can be chosen to be real-symmetric. This conjecture is central to understanding the subcritical regime: in the real-symmetric case, a proof would yield a detailed description of almost reducibility and hence of the dynamics in that regime.
record.source_name: Artur Avila, “Global theory of one-frequency Schrodinger operators I: stratified analyticity of the Lyapunov exponent and the boundary of nonuniform hyperbolicity”, arXiv:0905.3902 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.3902

record.title: Kawanaka's Macdonald polynomial conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ range over partitions, and let $P_{\lambda}(x;q,t)$ be the Macdonald symmetric function in the independent variables $x=(x_1,x_2,\dots)$. For a square $s$ in the diagram of $\lambda$, let $a(s)$ and $l(s)$ denote its arm-length and leg-length, respectively. For $a$ define the $q$-shifted factorial by

$$
(a;q)_{\infty}=\prod_{k=0}^{\infty}(1-aq^k).
$$

**Kawanaka's conjecture.** The following formal identity holds:

$$
\sum_{\lambda}\prod_{s\in\lambda}\left(\frac{1+q^{a(s)}t^{l(s)+1}}{1-q^{a(s)+1}t^{l(s)}}\right)P_{\lambda}(x;q^2,t^2)=\prod_{i\geq1}\frac{(-tx_i;q)_{\infty}}{(x_i;q)_{\infty}}\prod_{i<j}\frac{(t^2x_ix_j;q^2)_{\infty}}{(x_ix_j;q^2)_{\infty}}.
$$

This is a combinatorial identity for Macdonald symmetric functions, originally conjectured by Kawanaka in 1999. The paper's theorem proves the identity, so it is solved rather than open.
record.source_name: Robin Langer, Michael J. Schlosser and S. Ole Warnaar, “Theta Functions, Elliptic Hypergeometric Series, and Kawanaka's Macdonald Polynomial Conjecture”, arXiv:0905.4033 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0905.4033

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of May 2009); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Hamiltonicity hitting-time conjecture for edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles in random geometric graphs
record.statement:
Let $G(n,r)$ be the random geometric graph on $n$ points, and let $\rho_n(\mathcal{P})$ denote the smallest radius at which $G(n,r)$ has property $\mathcal{P}$. For a fixed $k\in\mathbb{N}$, write “there exist $k$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles” for the property that the graph contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles.

**Hamiltonicity hitting-time conjecture.**

$$
\rho_n(\text{there exist } k \text{ edge disjoint Hamilton cycles }) = \rho_n( \text{minimum degree} \geq 2k)
$$

w.h.p., for any fixed $k\in\mathbb{N}$.

Bollobás and Frieze proved the analogous hitting-time statement for the ordinary random graph. The assertion is known for choices of $(m_n)_n$ for which $G(n,m_n)$ has minimum degree $o(\ln n)$ with high probability, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Michael Krivelevich and Tobias Muller, “Hamiltonicity of the random geometric graph”, arXiv:0906.0071 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0906.0071

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2009). “This is known to be true for choices of $(m_n)_n$ for which $G(n,m_n)$ has minimum degree $o(\ln n)$ w.h.p. (c.f. ), but it is still open in general.”

record.title: Specht-dimension inequality for regularization and regularization-class minima
record.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a partition, and let $\mathcal{S}\lambda$ and $\mathcal{R}\lambda$ denote the two partition operations used in the source, with $S^{\mathcal{S}\lambda}$ and $S^{\mathcal{R}\lambda}$ their corresponding Specht modules. **Specht-dimension conjecture.** One has

$$
\dim S^{\mathcal{S}\lambda} \leq \dim S^{\mathcal{R}\lambda}.
$$

This is presented as a conjecture based on computational evidence in the context of constructing irreducibles indexed by the smallest partitions in regularization classes; its general validity remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: Comparison principle without strict extrema for the infinity Laplace equation
record.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be the domain under consideration. Assume that $u,-v\in\operatorname{USC}(\bar\Omega)$ and $f\in C(\Omega)$ satisfy

$$
-\Delta_\infty u\leq f\leq -\Delta_\infty v\quad\text{in }\Omega.
$$

Suppose that either $u$ has no strict local maximum in $\Omega$ or $v$ has no strict local minimum in $\Omega$. **No-extrema comparison conjecture.** Then

$$
\max_{\bar\Omega}(u-v)=\max_{\partial\Omega}(u-v).
$$

This would yield a comparison principle under the stated one-sided absence of strict extrema and, in particular, would support uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem when the source term is nonnegative or nonpositive. The source presents it as a conjecture motivated by a preceding comparison theorem; its resolution is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: The commutative loop conjecture for integer spaces
record.statement:
Let $IN=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$ and let $3^X$ be the integer space associated with $X\in 2^{IN}$. Define an operation $\oplus$ by

$$
A\oplus B\leftrightarrow A\cup B.
$$

**The commutative loop conjecture.** For all $X\in 2^{IN}$, $(3^X,\oplus)$ satisfies: (1) $(\forall A,B\in 3^X)(A\oplus B\in 3^X)$; (2) $(\exists !\xi\in 3^X)(\forall A\in 3^X)(\xi\oplus A=A\oplus\xi=A)$; (3) $(\forall A\in 3^X)(\exists !A^{\star}\in 3^X)(A\oplus A^{\star}=A^{\star}\oplus A=\xi)$; and (4) $(\forall A,B\in 3^X)(A\oplus B=B\oplus A)$. These conditions assert closure, an identity element, unique inverses, and commutativity. The conjecture relates the algebraic structure of integer spaces to non-associative finite invertible loops (NAFILs). The paper gives examples satisfying the conditions but reports no general proof or disproof.
record.source_name: Ivan Gatica Araus, “σ-Set Theory: Introduction to the concepts of σ-antielement, σ-antiset and Integer Space”, arXiv:0906.3120 (2010).

record.title: Uniqueness of the maximum-excess irreducible triangulation
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a surface, let $\omega$ be the largest integer such that $K_\omega$ embeds in $\Sigma$, and suppose that $K_\omega$ triangulates $\Sigma$. An **irreducible triangulation** is a triangulation with no contractible edge, and the excess is the quantity defined in the paper for triangulations of $\Sigma$.

**Uniqueness conjecture.** Suppose that $K_\omega$ triangulates $\Sigma$. Then $K_\omega$ is the only irreducible triangulation of $\Sigma$ with maximum excess.

By the extremal theorem cited in the source, this is stated as equivalent to the exact clique-bound conjecture. The results confirm it for $\mathbb{S}_0$, $\mathbb{S}_1$ and $\mathbb{N}_1$; the general case remains open.

record.title: Complete-graph containment in maximum-excess irreducible triangulations
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a surface, let $\omega$ be the largest integer such that $K_\omega$ embeds in $\Sigma$, and consider irreducible triangulations of $\Sigma$ with maximum excess.

**Complete-subgraph conjecture.** Every irreducible triangulation of $\Sigma$ with maximum excess contains $K_\omega$ as a subgraph.

For surfaces without complete-graph triangulations, the source notes that several irreducible triangulations attain maximum excess, making a direct characterization difficult. This conjecture proposes the common structural feature that all such extremal triangulations contain the largest embeddable complete graph.

record.title: Minimal mixed volume implies standard-simplex containment
record.statement:
Let $\Sigma_1,\ldots,\Sigma_m$ be an essential collection of integer polyhedra in $\mathbb{R}^m$, and let their mixed volume be $1/m!$, the minimal possible value. **Minimal mixed-volume conjecture.** There exist an automorphism $A:\mathbb{Z}^m\to\mathbb{Z}^m$ and vectors $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb{Z}^m$ such that

$$
A(\Sigma_1)+a_1,\ldots,A(\Sigma_m)+a_m
$$

are contained in the standard simplex. This is a structural claim about collections attaining the minimum possible mixed volume; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or remains open.

record.title: Topological invariants conjecture for maximal representations
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple Lie group of Hermitian type, and let $\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathrm{max}}(\pi_1(\Sigma),G)$ denote the maximal representation space. The topological invariants of Theorem~ are associated to these representations.

**Topological invariants conjecture.** If $G$ is not locally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Sp}(2n,\mathbf{R})$, then the topological invariants of Theorem~ distinguish connected components of $\operatorname{Rep}_{\mathrm{max}}(\pi_1(\Sigma),G)$.

For maximal representations into simple Hermitian groups other than the symplectic groups, this predicts that the available topological invariants completely determine the connected component. The source presents this as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.

record.title: Extremal-size conjecture for percolating sets in the hypercube
record.statement:
Let $m(G,r)$ be the minimum size of a set that percolates in $r$-neighbour bootstrap percolation on a graph $G$. For the $d$-dimensional hypercube $[2]^d$ and fixed $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the construction in Proposition~ gives an upper bound of order $d^{r-1}$.

**Extremal percolating-set conjecture.**
For $r \in \mathbb{N}$,

$$
m([2]^d,r) = \Theta\big(d^{r-1}\big).
$$

The conjecture asserts that the construction described immediately beforehand is close to extremal: its order of magnitude is the true minimum. The source does not state a resolution.

record.title: Conjectured sharp constant for Schatten-norm commutator inequalities
record.statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be general square matrices, and let $p,q,r\geq 1$ satisfy

$$
\frac{1}{p}\leq\frac{1}{q}+\frac{1}{r}.
$$

Write $\lVert\cdot\rVert_s$ for the Schatten $s$-norm, and let $c_{p,q,r}$ be the smallest constant such that

$$
\lVert[X,Y]\rVert_p\leq c_{p,q,r}\lVert X\rVert_q\lVert Y\rVert_r.
$$

**Schatten-norm commutator conjecture.** In the restricted case $p=q$,

$$
c_{p,q,r}=c_{p,p,r}=2^{\max(1/p,1-1/p,1-1/r)}.
$$

This is a proposed sharp-constant formula extending the Böttcher–Wenzel inequality to different Schatten norms. The source presents it as a conjecture based on numerical experiments; no resolution is supplied in the given text.
record.source_name: Koenraad M. R. Audenaert, “Variance bounds, with an application to norm bounds for commutators”, arXiv:0907.3913 (2009).

record.title: Edoukou's bound for intersections with a degenerate quadric
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}=\Pi_{n-r}\mathcal{Q}_{r-1}$ be a degenerate quadric of rank $r(\mathcal{X})=r$, and let $\mathcal{Q}$ be another degenerate quadric. Here $EH(r-1,q)$ denotes the previously defined upper bound for the intersection of two quadrics in $\mathbb{P}^{r-1}(\mathbb{F}_q)$. **Edoukou's degenerate-quadric conjecture.** If $r\ge 4$, then

$$
|\Pi_{n-r}\mathcal{Q}_{r-1}\cap\mathcal{Q}|\le EH(r-1,q)q^{n-r+1}+\pi_{n-r}.
$$

The bound is asserted to be best possible. The source notes that, if true, this determines the minimum distance of every functional code of order $2$ defined on such a degenerate quadric; no resolution is given.

record.title: The polynomial expansion conjecture for 0/1 polytopes
record.statement: A **0/1 $d$-polytope** is a $d$-dimensional polytope whose vertices lie in $\{0,1\}^d$. Let edge expansion mean the minimum ratio of boundary edges to the size of a vertex subset of size at most half the graph. **Polynomial expansion conjecture.** There exists a polynomial $p(d)$ such that every 0/1 $d$-polytope has edge expansion at least $1/p(d)$. This is one of two expansion conjectures described for 0/1 polytopes; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Finiteness conjecture for coconnected geometric distance-regular graphs
record.statement: Let $m\geq 2$ be fixed. A distance-regular graph is **geometric** if it has a family of Delsarte cliques whose incidence structure gives the graph, and it is **coconnected** if its complement is connected. For such a graph, let $\psi_1$ and $\tau_2$ denote the associated intersection parameters, and let the smallest eigenvalue be $-m$. **Finiteness conjecture.** There are only finitely many coconnected geometric distance-regular graphs with smallest eigenvalue $-m$ and $\psi_1\leq\tau_2-2$. This is the first of three conjectures proposed for geometric distance-regular graphs; the supplied text gives no resolution or further evidence.

record.title: The weight conjecture for free products of three non-trivial groups
record.statement: For a group $G$, its weight is the minimum number of elements whose normal closure is $G$. A free product is a group of the form $G_1*G_2*G_3$, where each factor is a group. **Weight conjecture.** A free product of three non-trivial groups has weight at least $2$. Since knot groups have weight $1$ and the weight property passes to homomorphic images, this conjecture would imply the two summands conjecture for Dehn surgery manifolds. The source states that this remains an open problem.

record.title: Generalized moonshine conjecture for the monster
record.statement: Let $\mathbb{M}$ be the monster, let $g,h\in\mathbb{M}$ be commuting elements, and let $\mathfrak{H}$ denote the upper half-plane. A **generalized character** is a function $Z$ associating a holomorphic function on $\mathfrak{H}$ to each commuting pair $(g,h)$. **Generalized moonshine conjecture.** There exists a generalized character $Z$ satisfying the following conditions: (1) $Z(g,h,\tau)$ is invariant under simultaneous conjugation of $g$ and $h$; (2) for any $\binom{a\ b}{c\ d}\in SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$, $Z(g^ah^c,g^bh^d,\tau)=\gamma Z(g,h,(a\tau+b)/(c\tau+d))$ for some constant $\gamma$ depending on the matrix; (3) for fixed $g$, the coefficients of the $q$-expansion of $Z(g,h,\tau)$ form characters of a graded representation of a central extension of $C_{\mathbb{M}}(g)$; (4) $Z(g,h,\tau)$ is either constant or a genus-zero function; and (5) $Z(g,h,\tau)=J(\tau)$ for all $\tau\in\mathfrak{H}$ if and only if $g=h=1$. This conjecture extends monstrous moonshine from the identity-twisted setting to commuting pairs in the monster. It remains open, although Borcherds's proof of the original moonshine conjecture establishes the genus-zero assertion for $Z(1,h,\tau)$, and other special cases have been resolved.
record.source_name: Scott Carnahan, “Generalized moonshine II: Borcherds products”, arXiv:0908.4223 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.4223

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2009). “This conjecture is still open, but some special cases have been resolved: Borcherds's proof of the original moonshine conjecture implies that $Z(1,h,\tau)$ is genus zero for all $h \in \MM$.”

record.title: Nash-Williams' Hamilton decomposition conjecture for regular graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$) be a $d$-regular graph on at most $2d$ vertices.

**Nash-Williams' conjecture.** $G$ contains $\lfloor d/2 \rfloor$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles.

Nash-Williams proposed this as a best-possible strengthening of the known lower bound for graphs of minimum degree at least half their order; the stated upper bound follows from the number of edges. The source does not provide evidence of resolution.

record.title: Binding number conjecture for Giroux torsion
record.statement:
Let $(Y,\xi)$ be a contact 3-manifold. The **binding number** $bn(\xi)$ is the minimal number of binding components among open books supporting $\xi$ whose pages have minimal genus. The **Giroux torsion** of $\xi$ is the largest $n$ for which there is a contact embedding

$$
(T^2 \times I,\xi_{2n\pi})\longrightarrow (Y,\xi),
$$

where $\xi_{2n\pi}=\ker(\cos(2n\pi t)\,dx+\sin(2n\pi t)\,dy)$. **Binding number conjecture.** The binding number $bn(\xi)$ of a tight contact structure is bounded below by the Giroux torsion of $\xi$. This would relate a combinatorial invariant of supporting open books to Giroux torsion, which is currently not visible from the open-book perspective; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: Darmon's refined class number formula for real quadratic fields
record.statement:
Suppose $F$ is a real quadratic field and $K_n=F(\boldsymbol{\mu}_n)$, where $n$ is prime to the conductor of $F/\mathbf{Q}$. Let $\theta'_n\in K_n^\times\otimes\mathbf{Z}[\operatorname{Gal}(K_n/F)]$ be Darmon's Stickelberger-type element, and let $R_n$ be the regulator defined from the chosen bases of the relevant unit and augmentation-ideal modules. Writing $\tilde\theta'_n$ for the image of $\theta'_n$ in $F(\boldsymbol{\mu}_n)^\times\otimes I_n^r/I_n^{r+1}$, let $s$ be the number of prime divisors of $n/n_+$, let $r$ be the number of prime factors of $n_+$, and let $h_n$ be the order of $\operatorname{Pic}(\mathcal{O}_F[1/n])$. **Darmon's refined class number formula.** For every $n\in\mathcal{N}$, one has

$$
\tilde\theta'_n=-2^s h_nR_n\quad\text{in }(F(\boldsymbol{\mu}_n)^\times/\{\pm1\})\otimes I_n^r/I_n^{r+1}.
$$

This is a leading-term refinement of the class number formula involving first derivatives of $L$-functions. The paper proves most of the conjecture using Kolyvagin systems, reducing the general case to $n=1$ and then to classical formulas; the stated leading-term identity is the conjectural form under discussion.
record.source_name: Barry Mazur and Karl Rubin, “Refined class number formulas and Kolyvagin systems”, arXiv:0909.3916 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.3916

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2009).

record.title: The canonical section conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras
record.statement:
Let $W$ be an irreducible complex reflection group, let $B(W)$ be its braid group, and let ${\mathcal{H}}(W,{\mathbf u})$ be its cyclotomic Hecke algebra with symmetrizing form $t$. A **section** is a map $W\to B(W)$, $w\mapsto{\mathbf w}$, whose composition with the natural projection $B(W)\to W$ is the identity; write ${\mathbf W}$ for its image. **The canonical section conjecture.** There exists a section

$$
W\to{\mathbf W},\qquad w\mapsto{\mathbf w},
$$

of $W$ in $B(W)$ such that $1\in{\mathbf W}$ and

$$
t(T_{\mathbf w})=0\qquad\text{for every }{\mathbf w}\in{\mathbf W}\setminus\{1\}.
$$

Such a section would provide a lift of the elements of $W$ with vanishing symmetrizing trace away from the identity, and is sought as a suitable basis for the cyclotomic Hecke algebra. The source does not give evidence of a general resolution.
record.source_name: Gunter Malle and Jean Michel, “Constructing representations of Hecke algebras for complex reflection groups”, arXiv:0909.4040 (2009).
record.references:

record.title: The 3x+1 maximum excursion constant conjecture
record.statement:
For the $3x+1$ map, let $t(n;\omega)$ be the maximum-excursion statistic in the repeated random walk model, and define

$$
\rho:=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log t(n;\omega)}{\log n}.
$$

**3x+1 maximum excursion constant conjecture.** The maximum excursion constant $\rho$ is finite and

$$
\rho=2.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the corresponding repeated random walk model theorem and its density estimates. The source does not provide a proof for the actual $3x+1$ map.
record.source_name: Alex V. Kontorovich and Jeffrey C. Lagarias, “Stochastic Models for the 3x+1 and 5x+1 Problems”, arXiv:0910.1944 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1944

record.title: Self-duality conjecture for finite Grassmann algebras
record.statement:
Let ${\mathfrak{B}}_{{L}}$ be the Grassmann algebra with $L$ generators, and write ${\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{ev}}$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{od}}$ for its even and odd parts. Let ${\bf{L}}_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{ev}}}({\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{od}}:{\mathfrak{B}}_{{L}})$ denote the set of continuous ${\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{ev}}$-linear maps from ${\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{od}}$ to ${\mathfrak{B}}_{{L}}$, meaning that $f(\lambda X)=\lambda f(X)$ for $\lambda\in {\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{ev}}$ and $X\in {\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{od}}$.

**Self-duality conjecture.** For every $f\in {\bf{L}}_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{ev}}}({\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{od}}:{\mathfrak{B}}_{{L}})$, there exists $u_f\in {\mathfrak{B}}_{{L}}$ such that

$$
f(X)=X\!\cdot u_f
$$

for every $X\in {\mathfrak{B}}_{{L},\mathrm{od}}$.

The claim is motivated by the expected self-duality of the odd part of a Grassmann algebra, but the paper states that Kazuo Masuda supplied a counterexample when $L=2$: the map defined by $f(X_1\sigma_1+X_2\sigma_2)=X_1\sigma_2$ is continuous and ${\mathfrak{B}}_{2,\mathrm{ev}}$-linear, yet no such $u_f$ exists. Thus the conjecture is refuted for finite $L$, while the paper suggests that self-duality may require countably many Grassmann generators.
record.source_name: Atsushi Inoue, “Definition and characterization of supersmooth functions on superspace based on Fréchet-Grassmann algebra”, arXiv:0910.3831 (2014).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.3831

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of October 2009); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Conjectured negative answer to the degree problem via equal admissible groups
record.statement:
Let the degree problem ask whether equivalent number fields must have the same degree. **Degree-problem conjecture.** The degree problem has a negative answer. Moreover, there exist a number field $M$ and a proper subfield $K\subsetneq M$ such that $K$ and $M$ have the same admissible groups.

This would produce a nontrivial pair of number fields related by admissibility while showing that admissibility equivalence does not determine degree. The source presents this as a conjecture and gives no evidence of resolution.

record.title: Approximation conjecture for almost commuting real symmetric triples
record.statement:
Let $H_1,H_2,H_3$ be real, symmetric matrices, and let $[H_i,H_j]=H_iH_j-H_jH_i$ denote their commutators. Let $I$ be the identity matrix. **Real symmetric triple approximation conjecture.** For all $\epsilon>0$, there exists a $\delta>0$ such that, whenever

$$
\lVert[H_1,H_2]\rVert,\ \lVert[H_2,H_3]\rVert,\ \lVert[H_3,H_1]\rVert\leq\delta,
$$

and

$$
H_1^2+H_2^2+H_3^2=I,
$$

there exist real, symmetric, pairwise commuting matrices $H'_1,H'_2,H'_3$ such that

$$
\lVert H_1-H'_1\rVert,\ \lVert H_2-H'_2\rVert,\ \lVert H_3-H'_3\rVert\leq\epsilon.
$$

This is an index-obstruction conjecture for triples: it asserts approximation in the real-symmetric setting without an explicitly nonzero index. The surrounding discussion contrasts it with the self-dual case, where a nontrivial obstruction is exhibited.
record.source_name: M. B. Hastings and T. A. Loring, “Almost Commuting Matrices, Localized Wannier Functions, and the Quantum Hall Effect”, arXiv:0910.5490 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5490

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2009).

record.title: Self-dual Bott-index obstruction conjecture for almost commuting triples
record.statement:
Let $H_1,H_2,H_3$ be self-dual Hermitian matrices, and let $[H_i,H_j]=H_iH_j-H_jH_i$ denote their commutators. Let $I$ be the identity matrix, and let $\widetilde{\operatorname{bott}}(H_1,H_2,H_3)$ denote the self-dual Bott index. **Self-dual Bott-index obstruction conjecture.** For all $\epsilon>0$, there exists a $\delta>0$ such that, whenever

$$
\widetilde{\operatorname{bott}}(H_1,H_2,H_3)=1,
$$

all three commutators satisfy

$$
\lVert[H_1,H_2]\rVert,\ \lVert[H_2,H_3]\rVert,\ \lVert[H_3,H_1]\rVert\leq\delta,
$$

and

$$
H_1^2+H_2^2+H_3^2=I,
$$

there exist self-dual Hermitian pairwise commuting matrices $H'_1,H'_2,H'_3$ such that

$$
\lVert H_1-H'_1\rVert,\ \lVert H_2-H'_2\rVert,\ \lVert H_3-H'_3\rVert\leq\epsilon.
$$

The conjecture concerns whether even a triple with Bott index one can be approximated by an exactly commuting self-dual triple. It is posed in the context of the paper's explicit index obstruction and is not resolved there.
record.source_name: M. B. Hastings and T. A. Loring, “Almost Commuting Matrices, Localized Wannier Functions, and the Quantum Hall Effect”, arXiv:0910.5490 (2009).

record.title: Kontsevich–Soibelman conjecture on $A_{\infty}$-pre-categories
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a graded commutative ring. An **$A_{\infty}$-pre-category** over $k$ has morphism spaces and higher products defined only for suitable transversal pairs and sequences of objects, whereas an $A_{\infty}$-category over $k$ has these operations for all relevant pairs and sequences. A quasi-equivalence is an equivalence in the corresponding homotopical sense.

**Kontsevich–Soibelman conjecture.** Quasi-equivalence classes of $A_{\infty}$-pre-categories over $k$ are in bijection with quasi-equivalence classes of $A_{\infty}$-categories over $k$ with strict (or weak) identity morphisms.

The conjecture provides the justification for replacing Fukaya $A_{\infty}$-pre-categories by quasi-equivalent actual $A_{\infty}$-categories, which is useful in the categorical formulation of homological mirror symmetry. The paper proves it for essentially small $A_{\infty}$-(pre-)categories when $k$ is a field, so the stated generality remains open.
record.source_name: Alexander I. Efimov, “A proof of Kontsevich-Soibelman conjecture”, arXiv:0911.0123 (2010).
record.references:

record.title: The crosscut lower-bound conjecture for diagramless link homology
record.statement: Let $k$ be the number of crosscuts, let $N$ be the number of copies of Khovanov homology in the diagramless homology of a link with $k$ crosscuts, and let the minimum crossing number of the link be the least crossing number among its link diagrams. **Crosscut lower-bound conjecture.** If $k$ is less than the minimum crossing number of the link, then $N=0$. This conjecture concerns the dependence of diagramless link homology on the number of crosscuts; the source gives no resolution or further evidence.

record.title: Generalized Montgomery conjecture for dynamic chromatic number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a nontrivial connected graph. Write $\Delta(G)$ and $\delta(G)$ for its maximum and minimum degrees, respectively, and let $\chi(G)$ and $\chi_2(G)$ denote its chromatic and dynamic chromatic numbers. **Generalized Montgomery conjecture.**

$$
\chi_2(G)-\chi(G)\leq 2\left\lceil\frac{\Delta(G)}{\delta(G)}\right\rceil.
$$

This conjecture generalizes Montgomery's regular-graph claim, since for a regular graph the degree ratio is $1$. The supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Arash Ahadi and Ali Dehghan, “Upper bounds for the 2-hued chromatic number of graphs in terms of the independence number”, arXiv:0911.4199 (2015).

record.title: The zero-location conjecture for fused transfer-matrix functions
record.statement:
Let $u$ be sufficiently small, with $|u|\ll 1$, let $s$ be a positive integer, and let $a\in\{1,2,\dots,s\}$. For each positive integer $m$, let $T^{(a)}_{m}(v)$ denote the transfer-matrix function defined in the preceding construction, and call

$$
\{v\in\mathbb{C}:\operatorname{Im}v\in[-\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2}]\}
$$

the physical strip. **Zero-location conjecture.** Every zero of $T^{(a)}_{m}(v)$ is located outside the physical strip.

This analyticity property is expected for the two-string solution that provides the largest quantum-transfer-matrix eigenvalue in the sector $N=M_{1}=M_{2}=\cdots=M_{s}$, based on numerical analysis for finite $N$, $u$, and $s$. The source gives no proof or resolution of the conjecture.

record.references:

record.title: Kaiser–Kráľ–King conjecture on fractional total coloring of high-girth graphs
record.statement: Let $\Delta\ge5$ be an odd integer. Let the fractional total chromatic number be the fractional analogue of the total chromatic number, and let the girth of a graph be the length of its shortest cycle. **Kaiser–Kráľ–King conjecture.** There exists $g$ such that the fractional total chromatic number of every graph with maximum degree $\Delta$ and girth at least $g$ is $\Delta+1$. The source explains that this conjecture was subsequently proved by the paper's main theorem, which establishes the weaker upper bound $\Delta+1+\varepsilon$ for odd $\Delta\ge5$; however, the supplied text does not state that the exact $\Delta+1$ assertion was resolved.

record.title: The superlinear blocking conjecture for general-position planar point sets
record.statement:
For a finite set $P$ of points in the plane, a set $B$ of points disjoint from $P$ blocks $P$ if every segment joining two distinct points of $P$ contains a point of $B$. If $P$ is in general position, let $b(P)$ be the minimum size of a blocking set for $P$, and let $b(n)$ be the minimum of $b(P)$ over all $n$-point sets in general position. **Superlinear blocking conjecture.** The minimum blocking number satisfies

$$
\frac{b(n)}{n}\rightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

This asserts that every general-position point set requires superlinearly many blockers; Pinchasi conjectured the stronger bound $b(n)\in\Omega(n\log n)$.
record.source_name: Attila Pór and David R. Wood, “On Visibility and Blockers”, arXiv:0912.1150 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.1150

record.title: The blocker number of simple drawings of complete graphs
record.statement: A drawing of a graph represents vertices by distinct plane points and edges by simple curves, with a vertex meeting an edge only at an endpoint. A drawing is **simple** if any two edges intersect at most once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. A set of points blocks a drawing if it contains no vertex and every edge contains a blocker. **Simple-drawing blocker conjecture.** The minimum number of blockers in a simple drawing of $K_n$ equals $2n-3$. A construction gives an upper bound of $2n-3$, while the general lower bound stated in the source is only $n-1$; the conjectured exact value remains open.
record.source_name: Attila Pór and David R. Wood, “On Visibility and Blockers”, arXiv:0912.1150 (2009).

record.title: The superlinear crossing-family conjecture for geometric complete graphs
record.statement:
Let $t(n)$ be the minimum number of colours needed to colour the edges of some geometric drawing of $K_n$ so that every pair of edges with the same colour crosses; each colour class is a crossing family. **Crossing-family conjecture.** The colouring number satisfies

$$
\frac{t(n)}{n}\rightarrow\infty\quad\text{as }n\rightarrow\infty.
$$

Since each crossing family can be associated with blockers, this is stated as a strengthening of the superlinear blocking conjecture and remains open.
record.source_name: Attila Pór and David R. Wood, “On Visibility and Blockers”, arXiv:0912.1150 (2009).

record.title: NP-completeness of planar linear arboricity at maximum degree four
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a planar graph with maximum degree $4$. Its **linear arboricity** ${\rm la}(G)$ is the minimum number of linear forests whose union is the edge set of $G$.

**Planar degree-four linear arboricity complexity conjecture.** It is NP-complete to determine whether

$$
{\rm la}(G)=2.
$$

The paper identifies this as the only remaining case in its discussion of planar graphs: the cases of odd maximum degree are immediate, maximum degree at least $9$ are settled by the main theorem, and the planar linear arboricity conjecture would settle maximum degrees $6$ and $8$.
record.source_name: Marek Cygan, Lukasz Kowalik and Borut Luzar, “A Planar Linear Arboricity Conjecture”, arXiv:0912.5528 (2009).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0912.5528

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2009). “However, despite many efforts, the conjecture is still open and the best known upper general bound is ${\rm la}(G)=\tfrac{d}{2} + O(d^{2/3}(\log d)^{1/3})$, due to Alon, Teague and Wormald .”

record.title: The linear-length monochromatic cycle conjecture for dense graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of sufficiently large order $n$, and let $0<c<1$. A **$2$-coloring** of $E(G)$ assigns each edge of $G$ one of two colors, red or blue. A **monochromatic cycle** is a cycle all of whose edges receive the same color.

**Linear-length monochromatic cycle conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G)>cn,
$$

then every $2$-coloring of $E(G)$ contains a monochromatic cycle $C_k$ for some $k\geq cn$.

This is presented as a seemingly easier conjecture than the preceding cycle-interval conjecture. It asks whether a positive minimum-degree proportion alone forces a monochromatic cycle whose length is at least the same linear proportion of the order; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Hao Li, Vladimir Nikiforov and Richard Schelp, “A new type of Ramsey-Turan problems”, arXiv:1001.2078 (2010).

record.title: Cusick–Stănică conjecture on the nonlinearity of a cubic rotation-symmetric Boolean function
record.statement:
Let $F_3^n$ be the Boolean function on $n$ variables defined by

$$
F_3^n(x_0,\cdots,x_{n-1})=\sum\limits_{0\leq i\leq n-1}x_ix_{i+1(\operatorname{mod} n)}x_{i+2(\operatorname{mod} n)}.
$$

Here, the **weight** of a Boolean function is the number of inputs on which it takes the value $1$, and its **nonlinearity** is its minimum Hamming distance from an affine Boolean function. **Cusick–Stănică conjecture.** The nonlinearity of $F_3^n$ is the same as its weight. The conjecture concerns the nonlinearity of degree-three rotation-symmetric Boolean functions, which is relevant to the construction of cryptographic algorithms. The source paper states that it proves this conjecture, so the claim is treated as solved.
record.source_name: Xiyong Zhang, Hua Guo and Yifa Li, “Proof of a Conjecture about Rotation Symmetric Functions”, arXiv:1001.2942 (2010).

record.title: Quadratic-size conjecture for k-blocked point sets
record.statement: A finite point set in the plane is **$k$-blocked** if its points are assigned one of $k$ colours such that two distinct points have the same colour exactly when some other point of the set blocks them. **Quadratic-size conjecture.** Every $k$-blocked point set has $O(k^2)$ points. The paper describes this as a strong conjecture; the largest known constructions are substantially smaller than quadratic, and no proof of the asserted upper bound is given.

record.title: Infinitely many $D$-Ramanujan graphs under the second-eigenvalue condition
record.statement:
Let $D$ be a degree matrix of order $t\geq 2$, let $T_D$ be its universal cover, and let $\lambda_2(D)$ denote the second eigenvalue of $D$. A finite graph with degree matrix $D$ is **$D$-Ramanujan** when its $(k+1)$-st eigenvalue is at most $\rho(T_D)$, where $k$ is the largest integer such that $\lambda_k(D)\geq\rho(T_D)$. **Second-eigenvalue infinitude conjecture.** If

$$
\lambda_2(D)<\rho(T_D),
$$

then there exist infinitely many $D$-Ramanujan graphs. This is a more specific proposed abundance statement for degree matrices satisfying the displayed spectral separation; the source gives no resolution.

record.title: The $2k+1$ threshold conjecture for maximal-chain trace extremal families
record.statement: Let $W(n,k,r)$ be the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{A}\subset [n]^{(k)}$ whose trace on every $r$-subset of $[n]$ contains no maximal chain, and let $n_0(k,r)$ denote a threshold beyond which the asserted extremal formula holds. **The $2k+1$ threshold conjecture.** For $k\geq r\geq 3$, Theorem~ holds with $n_0(k,r)=2k+1$. The preceding discussion gives a nonoptimal general threshold and suggests this sharper value; the source notes that $2k$ cannot work in general, since $n_0(3,3)=7$.

record.title: Maximum-attainment conjecture for minimal invariant convex sets
record.statement:
Let $S$ be an infinite, discrete semigroup, and let $\mathcal{C}$ be a weak$^*$-closed, convex subset of the cone of positive functions in $\ell^{\infty}(S)$ that is right-translation-invariant and minimal among all such subsets. Consider the intersection

$$
K(\beta S,\cdot)\cap K(\beta S,\diamond).
$$

**Maximum-attainment conjecture.** If this intersection is nonempty, then every function in $\mathcal{C}$ attains its maximum at every point in the intersection.

This statement is proposed as sufficient to prove the amenability conjecture above. Its resolution would therefore clarify whether the intersection of the two minimal ideals forces amenability.
record.source_name: Vern I. Paulsen, “Syndetic Sets and Amenability”, arXiv:1002.3157 (2011).

record.title: The Chern-class upper-bound conjecture for compact Lie groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a compact Lie group. Let $e(G)$ denote the invariant defined in the paper, let $n(G)$ be the minimal dimension over $\mathbb C$ of a faithful complex representation of $G$, and let $c(G)$ denote the rank of the central elementary abelian subgroup used in the definition of $e(G)$. **Chern-class upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
e(G) \leq 2n(G)-c(G).
$$

This conjecture would give a general upper bound for the nilpotence-related invariant $e(G)$ in terms of the smallest faithful complex representation and the central rank. The paper notes that the subgroup bound for finite $p$-groups is a special case, and develops a more specific conjecture about Chern classes of representations of elementary abelian groups that would imply this one.
